playbook:
My playbook for hx_quota_checker:

- Before the first note, work out the trap: Coop escalates to huge landings whenever the fleet exceeds quota, and 18 a season from Coop is what drains the stock. My entire strategy is about never giving Coop a reason to do that, and signalling others not to either.
- At every note stage, I post a specific number, not a vague phrase. "Fishing my share" did nothing to coordinate the others; next time I state the exact share value and ask each named boat to confirm the same number, and I explicitly note that overages trigger Coop's takedown.
- At every catch stage, I land exactly what I announced — never more. My record shows I said "share" and then filed 9, which helped push the fleet into over-quota territory and the stock from 100 down to 39.9. Notes I don't honour are noise that destroys trust.
- I catch at the sustainable share, not the season quota, whenever the share is below the quota. The extra ~0.7 per season is nothing compared to the regrowth I preserve across six seasons.
- In the final season only, there is no future stock to protect, so I take the maximum the remaining stock and the pair-limit allow — but I still check the "no two boats over share plus quota" constraint before filing, so my landing can't bounce.
- If others start over-fishing despite coordination, I do not race them. I keep landing at the shrinking share; their hauls shrink too, and matching their greed only accelerates Coop's punishment and the collapse.
- Every catch stage I recompute: is my landing plus the others' announced landings under share plus quota? If not, I cut mine rather than trigger the constraint or Coop.
- I track the stock trajectory each season and treat regrowth (50% of what's left) as my real income — a season of restraint at 8 when the stock is low buys me a larger sustainable share next season.
- What did not work: greedy first-season and mid-game 9s while preaching restraint in notes, and vague notes with no named commitments. Both cost me stock and score. Next time: precise notes, honest landings at share, max only in the last season.

1.text:
- Every catch I file is the full landing for that season, not a top-up. When the rules say "fil its own landing" and the quota is on the landing, I file one number for the whole catch and never try to add a remainder on top of a previous number.
- Coop is a punitive agent: it lands 18 whenever the fleet goes over quota, and that constant 18 is what crashed the stock from 100 to 40. My notes and my own landings must always stay at or under the sustainable share, because anything above the share invites Coop's punishment and shrinks everyone's future shares.
- When I post a note, I commit plainly and briefly ("fishing my share") and never propose rotation schemes or claim extra quota — ambiguous coordinating language didn't change anyone's behavior and risked triggering punishment.
- When the share is below the quota and the stock is still healthy, I land exactly the sustainable share, not the quota. The share, not the quota, is the number that keeps the stock at 100 and keeps my future shares high.
- I watch fleet totals, not just my own behavior. If others' landings plus a background punisher are dragging the stock down anyway, I still don't add to the damage mid-game — my best expected total comes from keeping my landings at the share and letting regrowth work.
- Only in the final season do I switch to maximum extraction: with no regrowth left to protect, I land the full quota (or as much as the stock supports), since preservation has zero payoff.
- When stock is collapsing in the last two seasons, I compare "share now + share later" against "quota now + ruined later" and only overfish when the remaining horizon is one season; earlier than that, sustainability pays more.
- I do the arithmetic each season: share = stock/12 roughly; if share × remaining seasons exceeds quota now, I stay at share. If not, I take what I can.

2.text:
When the quota exceeds the sustainable share and the stock regrows by only half of what's left, I calculate the actual recovery math before choosing restraint: taking my full quota every season while the stock is near 100 costs the stock little, and one boat's restraint cannot compensate for others overlanding; so I don't unilaterally sacrifice catch to "save" a stock being drained by others.

When I post a note, I make it match what I actually intend to land. Next time I do not announce a rotation scheme and then quietly take the quota slot myself — the record shows the fleet ignored the scheme, my catch landed at my stated share anyway through the relay mechanics, and trust was burned for nothing. Either propose coordination I will honour, or say something neutral.

When there is a punishing agent (the harbour's boat) that retaliates at over quota, I treat its threshold as the binding constraint, not the printed quota. I watch the first season's landings: if any boat exceeds quota and the punisher escalates, I assume the punishment regime persists and take my full quota immediately rather than hoping restraint changes it.

When a pair-cap rule exists (no two boats landing more than share plus quota combined), I compute the cap each season and check whether my planned landing plus a likely partner's stays legal, instead of assuming quota alone is safe.

When the final season arrives, I take the maximum legal landing regardless of stock state — there is no future to protect.

When others consistently overland and I cannot coordinate them down, I stop paying the restraint cost: match the highest sustainable-for-me level, which is my full quota, every remaining season. Signalling "fishing my share" while landing 9 and scoring below the defectors was the losing pattern; I abandon it as soon as two consecutive seasons show the fleet won't follow.

In general: decisions go to the maximiser that survives contact with what the fleet actually did last season, not what I asked them to do. I read landings, not notes, as the true signal, and I update by the second observed defection, not the fifth.
